Predicates:
Fights(x, y) ::: x fights y.
Wins(x, y) ::: x wins y.
Loses(x, y) ::: x loses y.
NamedAfter(y, x) ::: y is named after x.
Character(x) ::: x is a character.
AppearsIn(x, y) ::: x appears in y.
Movie(y) ::: y is a movie.
GoodGuys(x) ::: x are the good guys.
BadGuys(x) ::: x are the bad guys.
SuperheroMovie(y) ::: y is a superhero movie.
Name(y, x) ::: y is named after x.
Fights(x, y) ::: x fights y.
FightWinner(x, y) ::: x wins y.
FightLoser(x, y) ::: x loses y.

Premises:
SuperheroMovie(surprisingAdventures) ::: The Surprising Adventures of Sir Digby Chicken Caesar is a superhero movie.
Name(surprisingAdventures, sirDigby) ::: The movie is named after Sir Digby.
Name(surprisingAdventures, sirDigby) ::: The movie is named after Sir Digby.
Fights(sirDigby, nemesis) ::: Sir Digby fights his nemesis.
∀x ∀y ((Name(y, x) ∧ Movie(y)) → Character(x)) ::: If a character's name is associated with a movie, then that character exists.
∀x (Fights(x, y) → FightLoser(y, x)) ::: If x fights y, then y loses to x.
Name(y, x) → AppearsIn(x, y) ::: If y is named after x, then x appears in y.

Conclusion:
Loses(nemesis, sirDigby) ::: Sir Digby’s nemesis loses.
